**Checklist before reducing a Kafka topic’s retention**

| What to verify | Why it matters | How to verify (run‑book RB‑009 / incident notes) |
|----------------|----------------|---------------------------------------------------|
| **1. Identify the broker and disk that is full** | Retention only frees space on the *Kafka data* disk (`/data/kafka`). The root disk (`/var`) must be handled separately. | Run `df -h /data/kafka` on each broker (RB‑009 §1). |
| **2. Current retention settings** | Know the baseline you are shortening from (default `log.retention.hours=168` = 7 days if no override). | `kafka-configs.sh --describe --entity-type topics --entity-name <topic>` (RB‑009 §2). |
| **3. Consumer lag for the topic** | If any consumer group is lagging **more** than the new retention window, those messages will be deleted before they are read. | `kafka-consumer-groups.sh --bootstrap-server <broker> --describe --group <group>` and compare `CURRENT-OFFSET – LOG-END-OFFSET`. Incident INC‑0089 notes that “cutting retention below a consumer’s lag throws away unread messages.” |
| **4. Segment status (active vs. closed)** | Retention only deletes **closed** log segments; the active segment is never removed. If the active segment already contains > new‑retention data, you will still lose messages. | `kafka-log-dirs.sh --describe --topic-list <topic>` – look at `segmentSize` and `segmentAge`. RB‑009 §5 “Retention only removes closed segments. The active segment … is never removed.” |
| **5. Replication factor & under‑replicated partitions** | Deleting data on a broker that is already missing replicas can cause data loss. | `kafka-topics.sh --describe --topic <topic>` – check `UnderReplicatedPartitions`. |
| **6. Disk free space after the change** | Ensure the new retention will actually free enough space to get the disk back under the alert threshold. | Estimate space to be reclaimed: `sum(closedSegmentSize) – (newRetention * avgThroughput)`. |
| **7. No ENOSPC on the broker** | If the broker has already hit `ENOSPC`, it may stop writing new segments, causing data loss regardless of retention. | Look for “ENOSPC” in broker logs (RB‑009 §4). |
| **8. Apply the change safely** | Retention changes take effect without a broker restart, but they only start cleaning after the next segment roll‑over (default 24 h). | Confirm the change will be applied: `log.retention.check.interval.ms` (RB‑009 §3). |
| **9. Verify after the change** | Confirm that the disk usage is decreasing and that consumers are catching up. | Re‑run `df -h /data/kafka` and consumer‑lag checks after 24 h. |
